claim_boundary: C016 replaces the impossible arbitrary-circuit positive-only anti-checker route by a sound-circuit promise. H116 is open; no circuit lower bound or P-versus-NP result is claimed.

hypotheses.title: Sound-Circuit One-Sided SAT Anti-Checker Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: For every constant k there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, on input 1^n, outputs a polynomial-size list of pairs (F,a), where F is a satisfiable CNF of a canonically charged length polynomially related to n and a satisfies F, such that every Boolean circuit C of size n^k that is sound for SAT on the relevant input length—meaning C(G)=1 implies G is satisfiable—outputs 0 on at least one listed F.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: Any polynomial-size circuit family deciding SAT would be sound and complete. Choosing k above its size exponent would contradict the H116 list, so SAT would not be in P/poly and therefore P != NP.
hypotheses.proof_role: DIRECT_TARGET: preserve one-sided NP witnesses while explicitly restricting the quantified circuit class enough to exclude all-accepting and other false-positive supersets.
hypotheses.next_gate: Construct the list using only the semantic soundness promise, without testing circuit soundness, solving SAT, or allowing the list size exponent to hide the circuit-size lower bound.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H116 incorporates the C016 positive-only obstruction: arbitrary candidate circuits are replaced by circuits promised sound for SAT, while the constructor still uses only satisfiable formulas and assignment witnesses.
falsification_conditions: For some k, a size-n^k SAT-sound circuit accepts every formula in the produced list for infinitely many n.
The constructor needs to decide whether an arbitrary circuit is SAT-sound.
The total encoded list size or formula length makes the n^k comparison vacuous.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The soundness promise removes the constant-one counterexample but does not supply a construction. OPEN records only survival of the registered attacks.
